question: Following allegations made by the Government of Israel, in January 2024, that some UNRWA staff may have participated in the 7 October 2023 terror attacks, the UN Secretary-General, in consultation with the UNRWA Commissioner-General, set up an Independent Review Group.

The UN SecretaryGeneral also initiated a separate investigation by the UN’s Office of Internal Oversight Services to determine the veracity of these allegations. After nine weeks, the Review Group, led by Ms Catherine Colonna, concluded that ‘Israel has yet to provide supporting evidence’ for the allegations. 1.
Will there be any political or economic repercussions regarding the false allegations made by Israel?
Is the Commission ready to politically push for the recognition of the Palestinian state and work with the Council and Parliament to set this political will in motion?
Will there be any economic mechanism to help to rebuild Palestine, namely Gaza, like those created for Ukraine and the Western Balkans?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.3.2025) As highlighted by the European Council in its conclusions of 27 June 20241, the services provided by the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) are essential. The Commission therefore welcomed the report of the Independent Review Group appointed by the United Nations (UN) Secretary-General.

The EU has also welcomed the swift actions taken by UNRWA, further to the conclusion of the UN Office of Internal Oversight Services (OIOS), the UN highest investigative body in charge of the investigations against the staff accused of the participation in the 7 October 2023 terrorist attacks. Recognition of a state is not an EU competence, it falls in the remit of individual Member States.

On 27 June 2024, the Council recalled EU readiness to continue working with partners towards reviving a political process for a lasting and sustainable peace, based on the two-state solution, and to support a coordinated international effort to rebuild Gaza.

The Commission remains ready to explore how to support the early recovery and reconstruction of the post-war Gaza once conditions allow, and the overall prosperity and stability of the Palestinian people, including in the West Bank.
